short: An American unmanned aerial vehicle used primarily for intelligence gathering and precision strikes.
full:
The General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper officially entered service with the United States Air Force on 1 May 2007. Developed as a larger, more heavily armed successor to the MQ-1 Predator, it was the first hunter-killer unmanned aerial vehicle designed for long-endurance, high-altitude surveillance and precision strike missions. Operated remotely by a pilot and sensor operator, it can loiter over targets for over twenty-four hours.

The Reaper transformed modern asymmetric warfare by allowing continuous overhead monitoring and immediate precision strikes without risking a pilot's life. It has been employed extensively in counter-terrorism operations across the Middle East, Africa, and Central Asia, becoming the defining symbol of twenty-first-century drone warfare and sparking profound debates regarding the ethics of remote combat.
